analysis:
Integration review of the desktop-app 'Recommended for your Mac' per-chip ranking change. Replayed source shows recommendations.ts (chipEarnings, chipRanking, recommendedModels), contracts.ts types, StartServing.tsx, AutopilotModels.tsx, RecommendedModels.tsx, a test fixture, a changelog entry and docs. No provider process, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), key custody (A-002/A-003), prefix-cache (T-041), fan helper, add-on hold socket (TB-012) or installer (TB-013) code is touched.

Untrusted /v1/stats data is validated before use. chipEarnings requires networkEarnings freshness, by_chip_window '24h', an array for by_chip, a string chip, a safe-integer machines count >= 1, and digit-only amount strings before BigInt, so malformed input returns null and the ranking falls back to network totals. The `!` assertion on perChip.get in the sort is safe because it follows the mean > 0 filter. chipRanking keeps the ranking and its subtitle copy consistent. Output renders through React text interpolation with no raw HTML injection, so a hostile chip string cannot inject markup. The chip name is only compared to snapshot.machine.chip and printed in the subtitle.

Residual issues are low and pre-existing in kind. The coordinator (trusted) or a data manipulator could skew advisory earnings figures to steer model choice. The user still confirms, and the start action still selects from the eligible local model list. BigInt on very long digit strings is a negligible local CPU concern. The platform-side by_chip publisher and the Swift DesktopBackend /v1/stats relay are outside the supplied evidence. I identified no security regression and no required threat-model update.
